chunks: And from him, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Ajlan ibn Salih, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When you reach the Well of Maymun or the Well of Abd al-Sammad, perform ghusl, remove your sandals, and walk barefoot, and upon you be tranquility and dignity.'
And whoever sleeps after the ghusl, he must repeat the ghusl; this was narrated.

key_terms.بِئْرِ عَبْدِ الصَّمَدِ: Well of Abd al-Sammad, another well in Mecca
key_terms.بِئْرِ مَيْمُونٍ: Well of Maymun, a specific well in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What are the ritual requirements for entering Mecca according to the Well of Maymun hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the specific etiquette for entering Mecca, linking physical purification (ghusl) at the Well of Maymun with spiritual composure (sakinah and waqar). The requirement to remove footwear and walk barefoot symbolizes humility before the Sacred House, while the ruling on repeating ghusl after sleep underscores the state of ritual purity required for the sanctity of the city.
